Set up from your computer first

1. Settings, About phone: tap Build number 7 times.
2. Settings, System, Developer options: turn on Wireless debugging and Disable adb authorization timeout.
3. On the computer, open the Phonestick tray app and pair with the Wi-Fi code, then choose Set up phone. Or by hand:
adb shell pm grant %1$s android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
Open Quick Settings, tap the pencil (Edit) and drag the Phonestick tile in.
Switch access on and off without opening the app.
Lets Android wake the app the moment Wi-Fi or debugging changes, even when the phone is idle. Uses no battery: the app does nothing until woken.
None yet. Switch access on while connected to your home Wi-Fi: that network is remembered.
Plugging the phone into any computer or charger gives no access. Only your paired computer connects, over Wi-Fi, while access is on.
Only if access ever drops by itself: while access is on, quickly turns wireless debugging back on about every 15 minutes. Off by default.

While access is on, the app turns Wireless debugging back on whenever Android turns it off (Wi-Fi reconnects, reboots, moving between access points, idle timeouts), but only on approved networks. It does not run in the background: Android wakes it for a moment when the network or a debugging switch changes. It has no internet permission and no location permission.\n\nThe first time a new access point is used, Android asks \"Allow wireless debugging on this network?\". Tick Always allow once per access point.
